epistemic_status: historical model proposal/source fixture, never fresh replication

case.title: Small museum audio handset return
case.beneficiary: Visitors borrowing audio handsets and the reception attendant
case.valued_outcome: Visitors receive a ready handset with their selected language at the beginning of a visit.
case.success_measure: At least 95% of handoffs during the stipulated entrance period begin playback in the requested language within one minute.

hard_constraints.text: Use the existing twelve handsets and charging dock.
The reception attendant retains responsibility for admission; no added staff.
Do not collect visitor identities or persist listening histories.
Return handling must average no more than 30 seconds per handset.

case.incumbent: Returned handsets enter the charging dock and are handed out when their charge indicator is green. Existing partial mechanisms are green charge indicators showing battery readiness and laminated language cards helping visitors select the handset menu. The attendant relies on the preceding visitor's menu state until the next handoff.

observations.text: Synthetic handoff log: nine of 36 green-indicator handsets initially played the preceding visitor's language.
Synthetic timing record: eight of those nine handoffs exceeded one minute.
Synthetic return sample: checking charge alone took an average of eight seconds per handset.
Synthetic visitor tally: language choices were split among three menu options.
Synthetic menu trial: selecting a language from the home screen took 12 to 22 seconds in six trials.
Synthetic dock audit: four green-indicator handsets were sitting on a language submenu rather than the home screen.

unknowns: Whether submenu state contributes independently to delays.
How return timing overlaps with admission queues.
resources: Existing handsets, charging dock, language cards and timing sheet.
changeable_assumptions: Menu state is handled only at the next handoff.
case.provenance: Entirely authored synthetic preservation fixture; supplied sources are stipulations, not field observations or tested effects.

raw_candidates.claim: A return-to-home-screen step coupled with a visitor language choice before handoff could remove inherited language state and shorten menu navigation.
raw_candidates.delta: Treat menu readiness and requested language as joint handoff conditions alongside battery readiness.
raw_candidates.prediction: If inherited menu state causes delays, the pair may outperform resetting alone or advance choice alone; effects remain untested.
raw_candidates.probe: Compare paired steps, each step alone and existing practice across matched language requests. Stop if return handling exceeds 30 seconds on average.
assumptions: Reset returns reliably to the home screen.
Choice can be communicated without retaining visitor data.

raw_candidates.claim: Language-specific dock positions plus a visible menu-state check might reduce wrong-language handoffs by aligning location cues with actual settings.
raw_candidates.delta: Use location and verified setting together instead of charge indication as the availability cue.
raw_candidates.prediction: If location cues remain accurate, the pair may outperform dock grouping alone; uneven language demand could erase the benefit.
raw_candidates.probe: Compare paired steps with grouping alone under equal and uneven demand. Stop if admission work is delayed or visitor history is retained.
assumptions: Dock positions can be marked without replacement.
Setting checks do not consume admission capacity.
